text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- The latest decree on Gazprom, signed by President Boris Yeltsin on Thursday, ensures the rights of investors who have bought the company's shares before.
- A new gaz pipeline will be constructed to increase gaz supplies to Turkey according to a new contract with Russia's Gazprom.
- Russia's Central Bank is planning to establish more control over the activity of commercial banks.
- The fate of privatisation of Russia's biggest insurance company Rosgosstrakh is likely to be decided in court, says the paper.
- Russia's Defence Ministry is expecting a new wave of reshuffle.
- Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko has taken offence with President Boris Yeltsin over not being consulted in connection with the statement on retargeting Russia's nuclear warheads.
- The Second International television market opened on Thursday in Moscow with a presentaion of a new TV channel.
SEVODNYA
- The Lomonosov diamond deposit in the Arkhangelsk region will be put up for tender.
- The government is likely to increase excise duty for alcohol to 55,000 roubles from 45,000 per litre.
- Former Kremlin industry chief Oleg Soskovets is back into public life, seeking financial support for financial-industrial conglomerates.
- Afghan warlord Rashid Dostum has appealed to the Turkish government for help and is promising to return to Afghanistan, says the paper.
- Nearly 400,000 Russian prisoners will be freed under a planned amnesty if parliament approved the draft law.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- The mechanism of cutting budget expenses has been already set off and the State Duma's position on the issue will have little effect, says the paper.
- About 35 million pensioners are due to receive between 280,000 and 300,000 roubles per month while the rest 2,5 million are getting maximum pensions of 320,000 roubles.
- Belarus President Lukashenko says in an interview that he has got enough power in his republic and does not aim to vie for power in Russia.
- General Malik, who managed to push the Taleban militia out of the town of Mazar-i-Sharif on Wednesday, will not be able to maintain his control over the northern province, says the paper.
SOVIETSKAYA ROSSIYA
- The text of the Founding Act, signed in Paris, leaves no doubts that in essence Russia has surrendered to NATO.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- Moscow government is considering the question of doubling the underground and public transport fees.
- Russia has about 40 million tonnes of chemical weapons ammunition stored in seven regions but has no industrial technology to destroy it, says the paper.

- Russia could not prevent NATO expansion towards its borders and has to accept the real allocation of forces in the world arena, comments the paper on the signing of the accord between Russia and NATO countries.
KOMSOMOLSKAYA PRAVDA
- Raisa Nemtsova, the wife of First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov, gives her first interview and says she is not interested in politics.
--Tatyana Ustinova, Moscow newsroom, +7095 941 8520.
